15.text: But Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffereth him.

4.text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

7.text: Jesus said unto him, Again it is written, Thou shalt not make trial of the Lord thy God.

10.text: Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

17.text: From that time began Jesus to preach, and to say, Repent ye; for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

19.text: And he saith unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you fishers of men.

3.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

4.text: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

5.text: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

6.text: Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.

7.text: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

8.text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

9.text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called sons of God.

10.text: Blessed are they that have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

11.text: Blessed are ye when men shall reproach you, and persecute you, and say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.

12.text: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets that were before you.

13.text: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost its savor, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under foot of men.

14.text: Ye are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hid.

15.text: Neither do men light a lamp, and put it under the bushel, but on the stand; and it shineth unto all that are in the house.

16.text: Even so let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

17.text: Think not that I came to destroy the law or the prophets: I came not to destroy, but to fulfil.

18.text: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass away from the law, till all things be accomplished.

19.text: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

20.text: For I say unto you, that except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven.

21.text: Ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:

22.text: but I say unto you, that every one who is angry with his brother shall be in danger of the judgment; and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council; and whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of the hell of fire.

23.text: If therefore thou art offering thy gift at the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath aught against thee,

24.text: leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way, first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

25.text: Agree with thine adversary quickly, while thou art with him in the way; lest haply the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.

26.text: Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the last farthing.

27.text: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt not commit adultery:

28.text: but I say unto you, that every one that looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.

29.text: And if thy right eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body be cast into hell.

30.text: And if thy right hand causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body go into hell.

31.text: It was said also, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:

32.text: but I say unto you, that every one that putteth away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, maketh her an adulteress: and whosoever shall marry her when she is put away committeth adultery.

33.text: Again, ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:

34.text: but I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by the heaven, for it is the throne of God;

35.text: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

36.text: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, for thou canst not make one hair white or black.

37.text: But let your speech be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: and whatsoever is more than these is of the evil one.

38.text: Ye have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:

39.text: but I say unto you, Resist not him that is evil: but whosoever smiteth thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

40.text: And if any man would go to law with thee, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.

41.text: And whosoever shall compel thee to go one mile, go with him two.

42.text: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

43.text: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and hate thine enemy:

44.text: but I say unto you, Love your enemies, and pray for them that persecute you;

45.text: that ye may be sons of your Father who is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sendeth rain on the just and the unjust.

46.text: For if ye love them that love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?

47.text: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the Gentiles the same?

48.text: Ye therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

1.text: Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them: else ye have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.

2.text: When therefore thou doest alms, sound not a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

3.text: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

4.text: that thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.

5.text: And when ye pray, ye shall not be as the hypocrites: for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

6.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thine inner chamber, and having shut thy door, pray to thy Father who is in secret, and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.

7.text: And in praying use not vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

8.text: Be not therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

9.text: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

10.text: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.

11.text: Give us this day our daily bread.

12.text: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

13.text: And bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.

14.text: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

15.text: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

16.text: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen of men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.

17.text: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thy head, and wash thy face;

18.text: that thou be not seen of men to fast, but of thy Father who is in secret: and thy Father, who seeth in secret, shall recompense thee.

19.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal:

20.text: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

21.text: for where thy treasure is, there will thy heart be also.

22.text: The lamp of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.

23.text: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is the darkness!

24.text: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

25.text: Therefore I say unto you, Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than the food, and the body than the raiment?

26.text: Behold the birds of the heaven, that they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; and your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are not ye of much more value than they?

27.text: And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit unto the measure of his life?

28.text: And why are ye anxious concerning raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

29.text: yet I say unto you, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

30.text: But if God doth so clothe the grass of the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

31.text: Be not therefore anxious, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

32.text: For after all these things do the Gentiles seek; for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

33.text: But seek ye first his kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

34.text: Be not therefore anxious for the morrow: for the morrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

1.text: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

2.text: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured unto you.

3.text: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

4.text: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me cast out the mote out of thine eye; and lo, the beam is in thine own eye?

5.text: Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.

6.text: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast your pearls before the swine, lest haply they trample them under their feet, and turn and rend you.

7.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

8.text: for every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

9.text: Or what man is there of you, who, if his son shall ask him for a loaf, will give him a stone;

10.text: or if he shall ask for a fish, will give him a serpent?

11.text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

12.text: All things therefore whatsoever ye would that men should do unto you, even so do ye also unto them: for this is the law and the prophets.

13.text: Enter ye in by the narrow gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many are they that enter in thereby.

14.text: For narrow is the gate, and straitened the way, that leadeth unto life, and few are they that find it.

15.text: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.

16.text: By their fruits ye shall know them. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

17.text: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but the corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

18.text: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

19.text: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

20.text: Therefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

21.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father who is in heaven.

22.text: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy by thy name, and by thy name cast out demons, and by thy name do many mighty works?

23.text: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

24.text: Every one therefore that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them, shall be likened unto a wise man, who built his house upon the rock:

25.text: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon the rock.

26.text: And every one that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand:

27.text: and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and smote upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall thereof.

3.text: And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway his leprosy was cleansed.

4.text: And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

7.text: And he saith unto him, I will come and heal him.

10.text: And when Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

11.text: And I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:

12.text: but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast forth into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

13.text: And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And the servant was healed in that hour.

20.text: And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

22.text: But Jesus saith unto him, Follow me; and leave the dead to bury their own dead.

26.text: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.

32.text: And he said unto them, Go. And they came out, and went into the swine: and behold, the whole herd rushed down the steep into the sea, and perished in the waters.

2.text: And behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, be of good cheer; thy sins are forgiven.

4.text: And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?

5.text: For which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven; or to say, Arise, and walk?

6.text: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (then saith he to the sick of the palsy), Arise, and take up thy bed, and go unto thy house.

9.text: And as Jesus passed by from thence, he saw a man, called Matthew, sitting at the place of toll: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.

12.text: But when he heard it, he said, They that are whole have no need of a physician, but they that are sick.

13.text: But go ye and learn what this meaneth, I desire mercy, and not sacrifice: for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.

15.text: And Jesus said unto them, Can the sons of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then will they fast.

16.text: And no man putteth a piece of undressed cloth upon an old garment; for that which should fill it up taketh from the garment, and a worse rent is made.

17.text: Neither do men put new wine into old wine-skins: else the skins burst, and the wine is spilled, and the skins perish: but they put new wine into fresh wine-skins, and both are preserved.

22.text: But Jesus turning and seeing her said, Daughter, be of good cheer; thy faith hath made thee whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour.

24.text: he said, Give place: for the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth. And they laughed him to scorn.

28.text: And when he was come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus saith unto them, Believe ye that I am able to do this? They say unto him, Yea, Lord.

29.text: Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith be it done unto you.

30.text: And their eyes were opened. And Jesus strictly charged them, saying, See that no man know it.

37.text: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest indeed is plenteous, but the laborers are few.

38.text: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he send forth laborers into his harvest.

5.text: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and charged them, saying, Go not into any way of the Gentiles, and enter not into any city of the Samaritans:

6.text: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

7.text: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

8.text: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons: freely ye received, freely give.

9.text: Get you no gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses;

10.text: no wallet for your journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.

11.text: And into whatsoever city or village ye shall enter, search out who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go forth.

12.text: And as ye enter into the house, salute it.

13.text: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.

14.text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, as ye go forth out of that house or that city, shake off the dust of your feet.

15.text: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment, than for that city.

16.text: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

17.text: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you;

18.text: yea and before governors and kings shall ye be brought for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.

19.text: But when they deliver you up, be not anxious how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that hour what ye shall speak.

20.text: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.

21.text: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child: and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.

22.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.

23.text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone through the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.

24.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.

25.text: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his teacher, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more them of his household!

26.text: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.

27.text: What I tell you in the darkness, speak ye in the light; and what ye hear in the ear, proclaim upon the house-tops.

28.text: And be not afraid of them that kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

29.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? and not one of them shall fall on the ground without your Father:

30.text: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

31.text: Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

32.text: Every one therefore who shall confess me before men, him will I also confess before my Father who is in heaven.

33.text: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father who is in heaven.

34.text: Think not that I came to send peace on the earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.

35.text: For I came to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law:

36.text: and a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

37.text: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

38.text: And he that doth not take his cross and follow after me, is not worthy of me.

39.text: He that findeth his life shall lose it; and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

40.text: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

41.text: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward: and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.

42.text: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only, in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you he shall in no wise lose his reward.

4.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and tell John the things which ye hear and see:

5.text: the blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good tidings preached to them.

6.text: And blessed is he, whosoever shall find no occasion of stumbling in me.

7.text: And as these went their way, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to behold? a reed shaken with the wind?

8.text: But what went ye out to see? a man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they that wear soft raiment are in kings’ houses.

9.text: But wherefore went ye out? to see a prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

10.text: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, Who shall prepare thy way before thee.

11.text: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not arisen a greater than John the Baptist: yet he that is but little in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

12.text: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and men of violence take it by force.

13.text: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

14.text: And if ye are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, that is to come.

15.text: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

16.text: But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the marketplaces, who call unto their fellows

17.text: and say, We piped unto you, and ye did not dance; we wailed, and ye did not mourn.

18.text: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a demon.

19.text: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold, a gluttonous man and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners! And wisdom is justified by her works.

21.text: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

22.text: But I say unto you, it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judgment, than for you.

23.text: And thou, Capernaum, shalt thou be exalted unto heaven? thou shalt go down unto Hades: for if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in thee, it would have remained until this day.

24.text: But I say unto you that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

25.text: At that season Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding, and didst reveal them unto babes:

26.text: yea, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in thy sight.

27.text: All things have been delivered unto me of my Father: and no one knoweth the Son, save the Father; neither doth any know the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son willeth to reveal him.

28.text: Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

29.text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

30.text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
